messages:
Maria (support): FYI escalation from ACME (acct: acme-corp). They are seeing 502/503 when they should get 429 on quota hits for /v1/generate. Started ~2026-03-17T03:10Z. Customer is blocked, want SRE triage.

Maria (support): Sample request & response from customer:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-zzz' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hi"}'
```

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"quota-orch: upstream timeout","code":502,"trace":"trc-0a1b2c"}}
```

Maria (support): Customer says it only happens under traffic spike and when they exceed burst quota. They expect 429 with X-RateLimit headers.

Josh (eng-sre): On it. Can you paste the trace id? I want the quota-orch logs for trc-0a1b2c.

Maria (support): Trace id: trc-0a1b2c. Attaching log excerpt from customer request (sanitized).

Maria (support): ```
[2026-03-17T03:11:12Z] quota-orch request trc-0a1b2c incoming route=/v1/generate client=acme-corp
[2026-03-17T03:11:12Z] quota-orch -> auth-cache lookup key=acct:acme-corp timeout=1200ms
[2026-03-17T03:11:13Z] auth-cache timed out after 1200ms
[2026-03-17T03:11:13Z] quota-orch classifier fallback=upstream-timeout -> returning 502
```

Kevin (eng-runtime): This looks like the classifier treats dependency timeouts as upstream errors and returns 5xx. Expected behavior is to classify quota hits as 4xx (429). When auth-cache times out we should either: 1) return 429 if quota metadata indicates limit reached, or 2) surface a 503 but with a clear fallback that doesn't hide rate-limit semantics. Right now fallback path returns 502 which confuses customers.

Alyssa (prod-eng): Can we reproduce locally? Steps from support: repro with a burst of concurrent requests until auth-cache latency >1s. Maria, can you confirm headers (X-Client-Version) they used and concurrency?

Maria (support): They sent 50 concurrent requests from a single token over ~30s. Headers: X-Client-Version: acme/1.2.0. They used the hosted endpoint region us-west-2.

Josh (eng-sre): Quick checks I ran against staging: I pushed a short test that delays auth-cache and sent concurrent requests. I see classifier returning 502 when auth-cache latency crosses our 1s threshold. Repro command I used:
```bash
# slow auth-cache sim in staging
seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test' -d '{"model":"gpt-test"}' &
```

Josh (eng-sre): Staging logs: 
```
quota-orch: auth-cache lookup delayed 1100ms -> classifier fallback -> 502
```

Kevin (eng-runtime): Root cause: classifier logic treats any dependency timeout as an unknown upstream error and bubbles 5xx. That masks the underlying quota condition for downstream clients. We need two changes: short-term hotfix to prefer 429 when request context shows token exhaustion (best-effort), and longer-term: make auth-cache timeouts degrade to cached capacity info or fail-open to 4xx with a reason code.

Alyssa (prod-eng): For hotfix, suggestion: patch quota-orch to inspect 'quota-check' result. If we can determine 'exceeded' semantics (e.g., header or counter), return 429 with X-RateLimit.*; otherwise keep 502 but add explicit error code that support can map. Can we ship a patch today?

Kevin (eng-runtime): I can open a quick PR to change the classifier fallback policy to check last-known quota metadata. If last-known counters indicate limit reached, return 429. I'll also add a log flag to ensure we capture when fallback was used. Estimate 1-2hrs + rollout.

Josh (eng-sre): Operational mitigation: increase auth-cache timeout threshold in the routing policy to avoid transient 1s spikes triggering fallback, and enable circuit-breaker so that downstream requests get a deterministic 429 instead of 502. I'll coordinate config change.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy started for quota-orch hotfix branch "hotfix/quota-429-fallback" to canary (10% nodes).

Maria (support): Customer update template: "We're investigating and have identified a fallback path causing 5xx when quota checks time out. We're pushing a targeted fix to ensure rate-limited responses return 429. We'll follow up once canary is stable." Customer acknowledged and wants ETA.

Josh (eng-sre): ETA: canary within 30m, full rollout in 90m if metrics look good. We'll monitor 5xx->429 ratio and error rate.

Alyssa (prod-eng): Postmortem action items: (1) classifier logic unit tests for dependency timeouts, (2) add explicit quota-exceeded telemetry, (3) improve runbooks for support to distinguish 502 vs 429, (4) add regression test in canary for high-concurrency auth-cache delays. I'll create the issue.

Maria (support): Filed INC-4321 and linked PR. Will send customer update with ETA. Thanks team.

Kevin (eng-runtime): I'll follow up with the PR link and test logs.

Josh (eng-sre): Monitoring note: set alert if ratio of quota-orch 5xx to 4xx rises >5% over baseline during rollout.

Maria (support): closing thread here—I'll post final update when rollout completes.
